title: An arm64 Linux host falls back to Podman even though Firecracker supports aarch64
foundBy: session agent, while reading the engine default in internal/cli/create.go
details:
`defaultEngine` chooses Podman whenever `runtime.GOARCH != "amd64"`, and R112 in SPEC.md §12 makes that a requirement (`internal/cli/create.go:25`). So an arm64 Linux host with a working `/dev/kvm` gets a container sandbox and cannot ask for a microVM at all.

Firecracker itself runs on aarch64, and part of the support is already written. `fcArch` maps `arm64` to `aarch64`, and `fcDigests` carries a pinned checksum for the aarch64 release tarball (`internal/fcdisk/build.go:41`).

The guest side is what is missing, and the comment on the gate says so: the artifacts target x86_64. Two pieces would need work. The kernel build lifts an ELF out of Fedora's `kernel-core` with the upstream `extract-vmlinux` script, which is written around an x86 bzImage. `DefaultBootArgs` opens `console=ttyS0`, which is the wrong console for an arm64 guest.

The payoff is a real one: an arm64 Linux server, or an Ampere or Graviton host, is a plausible place to run a fleet of agent sandboxes. Nothing else in the tool is x86-only.
